name: Prophetic Vision (AVV)
body:
School divination; Level priestess (avv) 7, sorcerer/wizard 7th

CASTING

Casting Time see text
Components V,S

EFFECT

Range personal
Target caster
Duration instantaneous
Saving Throw see text; Spell Resistance yes

DESCRIPTION

The caster sees glimpses of the future. These are always difficult to interpret, as they are disjointed, disorganized, and out of context.

Prophetic vision brings to the caster’s mind information and images about the future of an important person, place, or thing. If the person or thing is at hand, or if the caster is in the place in question, the casting time is only 1d4 × 10 minutes. If the caster has only detailed information on the person, place, or thing, the casting time is 1d10 days, and the resulting lore is less complete and specific (though it often provides enough information to help the caster find the person, place, or thing, thus allowing a better prophetic vision result next time). If the caster knows only rumors, the casting time is 2d6 weeks, and the resulting prophecy is vague and incomplete (though it often directs the caster to more detailed information, thus allowing a better prophetic vision result next time).

During the casting, the caster cannot engage in other than routine activities: eating, sleeping, and so forth.

When completed, the divination brings prophetic visions (if any) about the person, place, or things to the caster’s mind. These may be forecasts that are about to occur, events that are far in the future, or deeds that someone is planning. If the person, place, or thing has no significant future, the caster gains no information.

The prophetic vision is always difficult to interpret as the images are seen out of context and out of sequence.

Any attempt to avoid or alter the foreseen events will fail, though the context in which they seem occur may be misunderstood or even altered.

For example, before heading into the mountains to search for a lost magical gemstone, the heroes cast this spell to see if they can anticipate anything. The GM knows there will be encounters with frost giants, a dangerous chasm to cross, and an NPC who confronts them, then helps them, and later betrays them. So the caster sees flashing, disjointed visions. In one, her companions are battling a frost giant, in another they are climbing steep slopes in a heavy storm. In another flash of images she sees her companions fighting a strange man, but later thinking him for his help.

When the caster later finds herself in the situations she foresaw in the prophetic vision, she experiences profound de-ja-vu and may gain some circumstance bonus or special insight into the situation (GM discretion).
